reference.source: Parsons' Diseases of the Eye 23rd Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Glare and glass changes mean cataract
Newborn white pupil operates in weeks
After cataract hazes later: YAG capsulotomy
Swollen lens plus pressure is phacomorphic
reference.pathophysiology: Lens crystallins oxidise and aggregate with age, steroids and radiation while fibre NaK pumps fail, hydrating cortex into spokes; galactose pathway dulcitol swells infant fibres reversibly, and rubella arrests developing lens leaving nuclear dust.
additionalDifferentials: Cortical versus nuclear versus subcapsular by glare and shift
Congenital versus senile by red reflex and age
Phacomorphic versus phacolytic by lens swelling versus leak
additionalInvestigations: Slit lamp typing with dilated fundus for surgical planning
Biometry with axial length and keratometry
